subject: LatticeCare MAP: cost playbook + gate questions (tokens/$, caching, batching)

Subject: LatticeCare MAP kickoff: initial cost playbook + gating questions

Jordan / Maya — attaching a first-pass cost playbook and a short snapshot of token economics for the MAP.  I put the high-level assumptions up front so the procurement and engineering teams can quickly validate.  Attachment: latticecare_map_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook) and token_econ_snapshot.pdf (one-pager).

Key assumptions (please call out anything that doesn't match your traffic):
- Avg generation tokens per API call (user turn): 550 tokens (prompt + model response).
- Baseline model: redwood/gpt-large-quantized equivalent; cost baseline ~ $0.0008 per 1K tokens uncached.
- Caching: prefix KV cache expected hit rate 35% in first 30 days; target 50% by steady state if frontend implements low-entropy prompts.
- Batching: recommend a soft batching window of 40ms with target batch size 6–12 for interactive throughput; burst windows for background inference up to 200ms with batch size 24.
- Evaluation plan: 2-week technical eval (synthetic + replay traffic) followed by 2-week pilot on production shadowing (no serving), then 1-week canary (10% traffic).

What we need from you to lock MAP milestones:
1) Confirm expected monthly request volume and % of long responses (>2k tokens).
2) Share 1 representative sample of user prompts (anonymized) so we can run prefetch and cache-hit sims.
3) Procurement: target decision date for SOW and capacity commit.

Quick worked examples are in the workbook but TL;DR for 10M calls/month (avg 550 tokens):
- Uncached: ~6.05B tokens/month -> cost @ $0.0008/1K = $4,840/month token cost (model only, excl infra margins).
- With 40% effective caching: tokens billed drop to ~3.63B -> ~$2,904/month.

Next steps I propose: 1) short call Mon 7/13 to confirm traffic profile and deliver updated workbook, 2) engineering sync 7/16 to review prefetched caching plan.

Thanks — happy to walk through numbers live.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jordan — quick worked numbers to bring to procurement.  Priyom and I did a short sensitivity table and put the snapshot also into token_econ_snapshot.pdf (attached).  Notes below are intentionally concise.

Assumptions: 10M calls/month, avg 550 tokens/call. Pricing model used: base model compute = $0.00065/1K tokens; platform & infra uplift = $0.00015/1K tokens; total = $0.0008/1K. We included 7% ops buffer for request overhead.

Scenarios (monthly token bill):
- No cache (0% hit): 10M * 550 = 5.5B tokens -> 5,500K units * $0.0008 = $4,400 (model/infra) + ops buffer = ~$4,708/month.
- Moderate cache (35% hit): billable tokens = 3.575B -> ~$2,860 + buffer ~= $3,032/month.
- Aggressive cache (60% hit): billable tokens = 2.2B -> ~$1,760 + buffer ~= $1,884/month.

50M calls/month (stress):
- No cache: ~27.5B tokens -> ~$22,000 + buffer ~= $23,540/month.
- 35% cache: ~17.875B tokens -> ~$14,300 + buffer ~= $15,301/month.
- 60% cache: ~11B tokens -> ~$8,800 + buffer ~= $9,416/month.

Batching guidance: for interactive flows where latency SLO <= 200ms, we recommend batching window 30–60ms and expected batched tokens per GPU inference is ~5–12 requests depending on concurrency shape. For background jobs latency >500ms, batch windows can be larger (200–300ms) and batch size 24–48 which materially reduces per-token cost (roughly 20–35% cheaper at 24+ batch size vs interactive).

Rollback/guardrails (canary):
- Metrics to watch: 95p latency, error rate, token burn deviation vs forecast (>15% dev triggers investigation), and user-facing quality regressions flagged by QA.
- Rollback trigger: sustained latency > 2x target for 5 minutes OR error rate > 1% for 10 minutes OR token burn > 25% vs baseline for 5 minutes.
- Sign-off: engineering lead @ LatticeCare + Redwood account lead (Ben) must approve.

We can convert these tables into a single-slide summary for procurement. Evelyn, I put a short note in the workbook explaining the buffer and uplifts.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
